newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open slightly higher.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open slightly higher Thursday in line with LME.
COMEX December copper was called up 0.30 to 0.50 cent from Wednesday's close of 90.35 cents a lb. It traded between 90.30 and 90.60 cents on ACCESS.
COMEX copper stocks fell 584 short tons Wednesday to 18,242 short tons, following a 8,626-tonne drawdown in LME stocks Tuesday to 220,950 tonnes.

The December/March backwardation narrowed slightly Wednesday at 1.00 cent, but has been widening from 0.50 cent on September 20, reflecting the tightness of the prompt market and the stock draws, analysts said.

Low fabricator inventories, limited scrap availability and prospects for seasonal demand strength should keep nearby futures above this year's low of 84.20 cents until there is evidence the market is shifting to a surplus supply situation, analysts said.
While the prompt market remains tight and the forward price curve remains backwardated, most analysts predict a global copper supply surplus next year.
